title: Defining Basic Interfaces
ques: Define a TypeScript interface named **`User`** with fields `id` (number), `username` (string), and `isActive` (boolean). Create an object adhering to this interface.
explanation: Interfaces act as structural blueprints, defining the exact properties and types that implementing objects must provide.

title: Using Optional Properties in Interfaces
ques: Create an interface **`Product`** where `title` and `price` are mandatory, but `description` and `discountPercentage` are **optional**. Show two valid instances.
explanation: The `?` modifier indicates optional properties, allowing flexible object shapes while maintaining type safety for properties that are present.

title: Immutable Data with Readonly Properties
ques: Demonstrate the use of the **`readonly`** modifier in an interface **`Config`** to prevent mutations after initialization.
explanation: Properties marked `readonly` can only be set during initialization and cannot be reassigned later, enforcing immutability in data structures.

title: Extending Interfaces
ques: Demonstrate interface inheritance by creating a base interface **`Vehicle`** and extending it into **`ElectricCar`** using the **`extends`** keyword.
explanation: The `extends` keyword allows interfaces to inherit properties from one or more parent interfaces, promoting DRY design and reusable contracts.

title: Type Aliases vs Interfaces
ques: Compare **Type Aliases (`type`)** and **Interfaces (`interface`)** in TypeScript. Explain declaration merging and when to prefer one over the other.
explanation: Interfaces support declaration merging and are optimized for OOP object modeling. Type aliases offer greater flexibility for union types and advanced type-level metaprogramming.

title: Defining Dynamic Index Signatures
ques: Write a TypeScript interface **`Dictionary`** that uses an **Index Signature** to represent a key-value store mapping arbitrary string keys to numbers.
explanation: Index signatures (`[key: KeyType]: ValueType`) allow typing objects with dynamic or unknown keys, while guaranteeing that all properties conform to the designated value type.
